summary: Prospect Hill fire tower, McKean County PA: built 1925, replaced 1967; top section moved to a Smethport museum yard, so not gone.

facts.status_note: Set for demolition in 2016. Only the top section was saved; it is on display at the Old Jail Museum in Smethport.
facts.agency: Pennsylvania Department of Forests and Waters

access.note: The salvaged top is on display at the Old Jail Museum in Smethport, which the McKean County Historical Society manages. No source describes access to the original hilltop.

events.note: Steel state tower completed in October 1925, 60 feet tall per the 1925 notice. The register dates the steel Aermotor tower to 1925.
First report of a watcher stationed in the tower. A 1925 notice had said an observer would be on duty in fire seasons.
Watcher reported the first forest fire of the season in the Open Brook region; Smethport crews were rushed to it.
Observer Frank Oviatt called in an April 1952 fire that threatened to burn up toward the summit; a large crew fought it.
A 1967 notice said the taller steel tower would be 82 feet 6 inches high and was under construction in the same location. The register says the tower was replaced in 1967.
Registered September 16, 2008, nominated by Henry Isenberg.
Tower set for demolition; efforts to keep it in place were unsuccessful, and the county allowed the top portion to be preserved.
Top section moved to the yard of the Old Jail Museum in Smethport. Sources say six or seven years to relocate it.
Restoration of the top section into an exhibit under way; two of four phases complete as of May 2024.

corrections.why: The top section was salvaged in 2016-2022 and is now on display in Smethport, so the structure is not fully gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 2022 newspaper says seven years of planning, fundraising and regulatory hurdles. The project page says it took six years to relocate the top section. The story reports both.

The register gives 2,435 ft (742 m) for the site, which the record keeps. A 1967 notice gives 2,495 feet for the hill, and a 1930 notice gives 2,560 feet for the tower. The story does not use elevation.

notes_for_editor: Record status gone is wrong: the top section was moved to a Smethport museum yard (2022) and is on display. Height 18.3 m matches only the 1925 tower (60 ft); the 1967 replacement was 82 ft 6 in (about 25.1 m). The top is inferred to be from the 1967 tower because the 2024 articles say the tower served nearly five decades (1967-2016). The record elevation 742 m matches the register, but newspaper figures differ. No source describes the hilltop today. The 2024 restoration status may be out of date. The register's 2008 nomination date is unchanged. No photos added.
